title: Aging‐Induced Ductile‐Brittle‐Ductile Transition in High‐Entropy Alloys and its Implications

recollection.starting_material: Guess: A cast and homogenized equiatomic CoCrFeMnNi high‐entropy alloy ingot
recollection.intervention: Guess: Isothermal aging at 500–700 °C for varying durations (10 h, 100 h, 1000 h)
recollection.structure: Guess: Precipitation of nanoscale L12-ordered γ′ and σ-phase particles within a face-centered-cubic matrix
recollection.mechanism: Guess: Initial ductile behavior controlled by solid-solution strengthening; intermediate aging induces brittle intermetallic precipitation at grain boundaries; prolonged aging coarsens precipitates and restores matrix ductility via crack‐deflection mechanisms
recollection.results: Guess: Room‐temperature tensile ductility dropped from ~60% elongation to ~15% after 100 h; fracture toughness K_IC fell from ~80 MPa·m^0.5 to ~30 MPa·m^0.5; after 1000 h aging ductility recovered to ~40% with K_IC ~60 MPa·m^0.5

score.note: The recollection correctly identifies thermal aging in an intermediate temperature range and mentions L12 ordering, but it uses the wrong alloy, omits the FCC+B2 microstructure and jagged phase boundaries, and incorrectly adds sigma-phase precipitation. Its grain-boundary precipitation/coarsening mechanism does not match the APBE, planar-slip, phase-boundary stress concentration, and ductile-transition-zone mechanism. The numerical tensile and toughness values are unsupported.
